newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products steady on firm bids.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products steady on firm bids.

text.p: Singapore oil products were steady to firmer on Wednesday along with a rise in crude prices, traders said.

They said physical gas oil was supported by trade buying with a US trader selling 150,000 barrels for Nov 25-29 lifting fob to a Singapore trader. Some traders had initially anticipated that gas oil values would dip under $30.00 per barrel especially after swaps gas oil slipped to $29.65/$29.75, down 5-10 cents from Tuesday. The market was concerned by talk of anticipated arrival of several cargoes from the U.S. West Coast in late December and January.
Sri Lanka has issued a tender to sell 120,000 barrels of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel and 80,000 barrels of jet fuel for December 12-13 delivery, which closes November 13.

Pakistan's first quarter 1997 tender to buy diesel, fuel oil and gasoline would only be known by November 15 after the new oil minister under the country's caretaker government reviews its oil import policy, an official said.

Jet fuel was offered by two majors at parity to Singapore quotes for end-November lifting and at $30.15 for Nov 22-26 lifting. This reflected the selling pressure the jet fuel market is experiencing and prices should dip further, traders said.

Gasoline activity was stymied as traders awaited results from Taiwan's December reformate tender. By market close, Taiwan bought 750,000 barrels - one leaded and two unleaded 95-octane cargoes - at around $25.50 a barrel c+f. Taiwan cancelled its leaded requirement in its last tender due to high spot prices but bought two unleaded for Nov 21-30/Dec 1-15 arrival at $25.90. December swaps offers fell to $24.70 from $25 Tuesday. Fuel oil prices firmed as buyers emerged. S.Korean supplies were sold out for Nov with a Korean refiner saying that refineries are running more low sulphur crude to produce light end products for winter stockpile.--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3084)
